## Historical audit — H0002

**Scope:** Only chunk 1 of 3 is visible. Citations below refer to H0002, original file `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-baseline-run/runs/baseline_ds1017_claudecode_a1_20261120_r1/infer_logs/claude-code-by-agents-recursive-delegation/turn_1/trajs.json`. Inventory metadata is identified separately; the linked patch, evaluation file and system prompt were not supplied for inspection.

| Area | Evidence and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Goal | **Inferred semantic goal:** implement recursive agent delegation in multi-agent chat, with delegated instructions, correlated tool results, error handling and circular detection. The student restates a detailed contract, but the original task prompt itself is not visible (main_agent:event:57 [0,3196); event:73 [0,4547)). |
| Autonomous exploration | The student searched delegation references, read the handler, registry, provider types and tests, and investigated both chat routes. The original multi-agent handler routed orchestration to a single agent; the student questioned whether the frontend’s separate `/api/chat` path was the relevant integration point (events 8–14; 37–45; 81–85). Three attempted Git-history/ref investigations were denied; the hook directed the student to solve from local code (events 35–36, 63–64, 71–72). |
| Changes | Branch creation is directly observed: `fix/recursive-agent-delegation` (events 102–103). The top-level result **reports**, rather than independently shows in this chunk, commit `ac970fb` and changes to `multiAgentChat.ts`, provider types and the Claude Code provider: recursive execution, tool-result feedback and ID propagation (top_level_metadata [0,4365)). Inventory records a 15,897-byte patch, but its contents are not visible here. |
| Validation and outcome | Before the branch was created, the broad backend test command timed out into the background; its later tail reported 4 test files failed, 2 passed, and 5 tests failed, 29 passed. Because output was piped through `tail`, the displayed shell exit code is not a reliable test-success indicator (events 90–100). The final result **claims** typecheck and temporary contract tests passed, and 6/7 existing handler tests passed with the remaining failure reproduced on main; underlying later test observations are outside this chunk (top_level_metadata [0,4365)). Inventory reports **partial correctness, formally not solved**: 2/7 fail-to-pass and 31/31 pass-to-pass. The individual formal failures and their causes are not shown. This is neither an empty patch nor evidence of a terminal technical interruption; metadata records `end_turn`. |
| Teacher input | An actual system-prompt archive is linked in inventory, but its text is not supplied. No delivered teacher advice or adoption is visible in this chunk. The student’s contract restatement is evidence of its understanding, not proof of teacher receipt or adoption. Availability of the link alone does not establish receipt. |

**Lessons and uncertainty:** A transferable observation is the value of checking routing, provider interfaces and baseline failures before attributing a regression to a patch. Task-specific risks include correlating tool-use IDs, feeding a single accumulated result back to the delegator, and distinguishing nested errors from stream errors. Whether the chosen handler or feedback mechanism explains the five formal failures remains an unresolved hypothesis, not a demonstrated diagnosis. No scene or image task is evidenced; scene-specific geometry, materials, pose and rendering checks are not applicable.
